statements.t: Our record year-to-date performance has us on track for another outstanding year.
The company now estimates reported sales growth for full-year 2026 of 48 to 49 percent versus prior guidance of 37 to 39 percent.

The company now expects full-year 2026 EPS of $4.54 to $4.57 on a GAAP basis and adjusted EPS of $5.36 to $5.39, versus prior guidance of $4.29 to $4.39 on a GAAP basis and adjusted EPS of $5.00 to $5.10.
A live audio webcast of the conference call and materials will be available through the “Investor Relations” section of the company’s website (http://investors.nvent.com).
The Company believes that these non-GAAP financial measures will be useful to investors as well to assess the continuing strength of the Company's underlying operations.
We have taken pricing actions and implemented supply chain optimization and other productivity improvements to help offset expected cost increases and mitigate potential supply chain constraints.

The potential impact of inflationary increases, including impacts related to tariffs, and supply chain constraints remains uncertain, but we expect those macroeconomic conditions will likely continue throughout 2026 and beyond, which could negatively impact our results of operations.
We expect these megatrends to continue and drive sales growth throughout 2026 and beyond.
We expect continued investment in new products to further drive sales growth throughout 2026 and beyond.
We expect to continue to have cash requirements to support working capital needs and capital expenditures, to pay interest and service debt and to pay dividends to shareholders quarterly.

risks.t: adverse effects on our business operations or financial results, including the overall global economic and business conditions impacting our business
the ability to achieve the benefits of our restructuring plans
the ability to successfully identify, finance, complete and integrate acquisitions, including the Maverick Power acquisition
competition and pricing pressures in the markets we serve
volatility in currency exchange rates, interest rates and commodity prices
inability to generate savings from excellence in operations initiatives consisting of lean enterprise, supply management and cash flow practices
inability to mitigate material and other cost inflation
risks related to the availability of, and cost inflation in, supply chain inputs, including labor, raw materials, commodities, packaging and transportation
increased risks associated with operating foreign businesses
risks associated with or arising from military conflicts
the ability to deliver backlog and win future project work
failure of markets to accept new product introductions and enhancements
the impact of changes in laws and regulations, including those that limit U.S. tax benefits
the outcome of litigation and governmental proceedings
the ability to achieve our long-term strategic operating goals

estimates.t: We have adopted various accounting policies to prepare the consolidated financial statements in accordance with GAAP.
